leading_positions.synthesis: All eight round-1 files give B009 (optical lattice clocks, Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye) as the sole prize part of the preferred configuration. Five members moved to it from a different opening first choice (Danielsson from B050, Eriksson from B018, Johansson from B008, Mehlig from B005, Pearce from B052). Their shared reasons are independent reproduction at RIKEN, JILA, PTB, NIST and SYRTE, a two-name credit with separable roles (Katori for the magic-wavelength concept and first realization, Ye for record accuracy and many-body physics), and consequences such as millimetre-scale redshift, constant-drift bounds and the prospective redefinition of the second. What is not shared: the citation wording (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce cite the 10^-18 level, Mehlig anchors on magic-wavelength trapping, Danielsson on a new regime of precision, Olsson on enabling 1e-18 clocks), how much weight the 2005 and 2012 precedents carry, and each member's reserve choice. The files show agreement on a preferred configuration, not a ruling.

areas_of_agreement: All eight files prefer a single-part prize for B009 with exactly Katori and Ye as laureates; no file proposes a second part alongside it.
Members describe the empirical case as mature: independently built Sr, Yb and Hg clocks in several laboratories are reproduced and compared at about the 1e-18 level.

Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson say the citation should rest on the magic-wavelength lattice invention and realization, not on clock accuracy in general, so that the 2005 frequency-comb prize is not honoured a second time.

Members judged B008, B018 and B001 not ready to lead this year because of open credit questions (Wallraff, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Chu respectively omitted), and several raised the WMAP versus Planck and Puget question for B050.
Danielsson and Lindroth, who considered a second part, found none that pairs cleanly with B009 under the three-name limit.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus instrument: Johansson notes no departure from known physics has yet been seen, Danielsson says a prize about better numbers risks looking incremental, and Eriksson ranked B009 sixth in the opening because it is not a new state of matter; Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson reply that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct principle and that the redshift, constant-drift and many-body results are physics in their own right.

Novelty against the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control and ion-clock prizes: all eight files raise it as the main reservation. Eriksson is less relaxed about 2012 than about 2005; Danielsson and Johansson note that the lattice clock relies on the comb for frequency readout.

Reserve choices diverge: B010 is named as an alternative by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce; B018 and B019 by Eriksson and Olsson; B008 by Danielsson and Johansson; B001 by Kroll and Lindroth; B050 by Danielsson; B005 by Mehlig; B052 by Pearce.

IceCube (B052): the diffuse flux is established and TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 give independent routes, but Pearce, Danielsson and Olsson regard source identification as still maturing, and Olsson notes some associations are only at 3 to 4 sigma.
attribution_disputes: For B009, Lemonde and SYRTE, Ludlow, Oates, Takamoto, Hinkley, Bloom, Lisdat and PTB are cited as contributors outside the two names. Danielsson, Johansson and Lindroth judge the Katori and Ye roles separable and the two-name credit safe; Olsson and Kroll want the priority history checked, and both say they are relying partly on memory.

Olsson asks whether the invention credit rests on Katori's proposal and first demonstration or also on Ye's accuracy and stability milestones. Pearce asks whether Ye's decisive contribution is the lattice clock itself or the wider JILA programme (comb-linked spectroscopy, spin-exchange physics), and whether Hall's earlier role bears on allocation.
Lindroth states that within the atomic community the magic-wavelength priority is not seriously contested as Katori's; this is a member statement that no file independently checks.

Alternatives: B008 omits Wallraff (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson); B018 omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce); B019 omits Yuan Cao (Eriksson, Olsson); B001 omits Chu and has contested Bordé, Pritchard and Kasevich priority (Kroll, Lindroth); B050 has the WMAP versus Planck and Puget question (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce); B052 cannot represent the collaboration or credit the AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND pioneers (Pearce, Olsson); B010 requires choosing three of four names (Kroll, Lindroth).
maturity_disputes: The redefinition of the second has not happened. Danielsson reads it as making the timing right; Pearce says it is a consequence rather than part of the discovery, so the citation should not depend on it; Kroll asks whether it and the new-physics searches count as realised or still prospective impact.

Circuit QED (B008): Johansson presents it as mature and reproduced over about twenty years, while Danielsson, Kroll, Mehlig and Olsson worry about its closeness in time to the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
B019: Mehlig says only about eight years have passed and the pairing mechanism is unsettled; Eriksson and Olsson also note the unsettled origin of its superconductivity.
B005: Kroll doubts the quantitative confirmation of the flocking-transition exponents, and Mehlig records the confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents as only partial.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology at Chalmers; co-author of the dynamical Casimir experiment in superconducting circuits with Delsing and Wilson; Chalmers hosted 2025 laureates Martinis and Clarke as guests) flags a possible conflict for B008, and more loosely B003 and other superconducting-circuit work, and says he would recuse or defer. He reports no tie to the B009, B010 or B018 names.

Kroll reports membership of the WACQT management team, overlapping institutionally with Johansson, so he would not push B008. He also notes a year of his PhD in John Hall's lab in Boulder, a loose link to the JILA environment of Jun Ye, flagged for the record and not considered disqualifying for B009.
Lindroth reports close collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and attosecond groups, none involved in her preferred configuration, and no collaboration with Katori or Ye.
Danielsson flags his Princeton PhD under David Gross in case the committee wishes to consider it for B050.

Olsson and Mehlig disclose only that they are Chalmers or Gothenburg colleagues of Johansson, and Eriksson only scientific closeness to B018 and B019; none reports a personal tie to a credited name. Pearce, the Chair, records general field closeness to B052 (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur membership) with no personal connection to its credited people, and B052 was his opening first place.
questions_for_round2: Citation: what wording makes the magic-wavelength lattice and many-atom interrogation the stated new element, distinct from the 2005 frequency comb and the 2012 ion-control prizes, and should the 1e-18 figure or the redefinition of the second appear in it at all?

Precedent: do Eriksson and Mehlig (opening rank six) and Pearce (opening rank three), after reading the replies, still regard the 2005 and 2012 overlap as a reason to hold B009 back, and what evidence would settle it for them?

Credit: can the members and outside experts establish who demonstrated what first (Katori's proposal and first demonstration against the JILA accuracy and many-body milestones, and the roles of SYRTE, PTB, NIST and RIKEN), and does that support a two-name credit that leaves out Lemonde, Ludlow, Oates and Takamoto?
Ye's role: is Jun Ye credited for the lattice-clock realization specifically or for the wider JILA programme, and does Hall's 2005 prize affect how his share is framed?

Structure: would any member support a second, distinct prize part alongside B009, and if so which candidate and with which named laureates, given that no member has shown that one fits under the three-name limit?

Reserve: if B009 were set aside, which single alternative would each member put first, given that B010 has the most explicit reserve endorsements (five) but requires choosing three of four names, and the others each carry an open credit or timing question (Wallraff for B008, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang for B018, Cao for B019, Chu for B001, Planck and Puget for B050, collaboration scope for B052)?

Process: should Johansson be formally recused on B008 if it returns, should Kroll step back from advocating it, and which independent evaluations (clock lineage, the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, Wallraff, IceCube credit) should be requested before the final ballot?
summary.chair_observation: All eight round-1 files prefer B009 with Katori and Ye as the whole configuration, and five members moved to it from a different opening first choice. The shared reasoning concerns independent reproduction, a clean two-name credit and distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, while the open points are the citation wording, the credit of other lattice-clock groups and the weight of the pending redefinition of the second. Reserve choices diverge and each carries an unresolved credit or timing question. Round 2 should test the overlap and priority questions against evidence rather than treat the apparent agreement as settled.
